concept.name: Execution-enabled trading agent
concept.definition: A trading agent with the technical capability to submit, modify, or cancel orders on a market — the category of automation that pre-trade risk controls exist to govern. Under SEC Rule 15c3-5, any broker-dealer providing such market access must maintain automated financial and regulatory risk management controls — credit/capital thresholds, erroneous-order prevention, restricted-security checks — under its direct and exclusive control.
concept.intuition: The moment an agent can touch the order book, it stops being software and starts being market access — with the same regulatory obligations and blow-up potential as any automated trading system.
concept.mechanics: The agent holds order-routing credentials; every order it generates passes through mandatory pre-trade risk checks (size, price, credit, duplicates, restricted lists) before reaching the exchange or ATS, and executions are reported to surveillance in real time. The control layer must be documented, tested annually, and certified by the CEO under 15c3-5(e).
concept.failure_modes: Failure modes compound the model's and the market's: hallucinated or injected instructions become real orders at machine speed, and feedback loops between an errant agent and a moving market can amplify losses before humans react. Kill switches and throttles bound the blast radius but cannot prevent the first bad orders.
concept.misconceptions: A paper-trading track record does not certify an execution-enabled agent — live order flow faces slippage, partial fills, and market impact the simulation may omit. 'The strategy is good' is not an argument against mandatory pre-trade controls; the controls exist for when the agent is wrong or compromised.
concept.example: An execution agent managing a futures portfolio can submit orders only through a gateway enforcing 15c3-5-style checks: per-order size caps, daily loss limits, fat-finger price bands, and a restricted list excluding illiquid contracts.

citations.source: 17 CFR § 240.15c3-5, Risk management controls for brokers or dealers with market access (SEC Market Access Rule)
citations.section: Paragraphs (b)-(e): controls, direct and exclusive control, annual review and CEO certification
